_comment: CryptoSureEdu demo question bank. Placeholder questions written for the demo, three per module. 'correctOption' is the index (starting at 0) of the right answer. The answer key sits in this public file only because this is a demo; a real deployment keeps the key server-side and draws questions from a larger pool.

questions.prompt: A website you have never used asks you to connect your wallet and approve unlimited spending of a token. What is the safe response?
options: Approve it; approvals cost nothing
Decline, and only approve amounts you intend to spend on sites you trust
Approve it, then disconnect the wallet afterwards

questions.prompt: Why keep long-term holdings in a different wallet from the one you use for day-to-day apps?
options: So one bad signature cannot reach everything you own
Because wallets slow down when they hold more assets
It lowers network fees

questions.prompt: Before signing a transaction, what should you check?
options: Only the network fee
Nothing; the app has already checked it
The destination address, the amount, and what the transaction is allowed to do
A fall in the market price of your assets
An unauthorized transfer out of the insured wallet
Any loss on any wallet you own

questions.prompt: The policy is bound to how many wallets?
options: One: the wallet you proved you control when you applied
Every wallet derived from your seed phrase
Any wallet you nominate at claim time

questions.prompt: If your holdings grow above the policy limit, a covered loss pays:
options: The full value of the holdings
Nothing, because the wallet is over the limit
Up to the policy limit, less the deductible

questions.prompt: Someone claiming to be wallet support messages you and asks for your seed phrase to 'verify your account'. What do you do?
options: Send it; support needs it to help
Send only the first six words
Refuse. No legitimate service ever asks for a seed phrase

questions.prompt: What is the most reliable way to reach a site you use for crypto?
options: A bookmark you saved yourself, or typing the address
The top sponsored search result
A link in an urgent email

questions.prompt: An unexpected token appears in your wallet with a link in its name promising a reward. You should:
options: Visit the link to claim it
Leave it alone and not interact with it
Send it to a friend to test

questions.prompt: Where is an acceptable place to keep a seed phrase?
options: A photo in your cloud storage
Written down offline and stored somewhere physically secure
A note in your email drafts

questions.prompt: Anyone who learns your seed phrase can:
options: Only view your balances
Do nothing without your device
Recreate your wallet and move everything in it

questions.prompt: Why keep more than one offline copy of a seed phrase, in separate places?
options: So a single fire, flood or theft does not destroy your only copy
Because copies expire
To share access with customer support

questions.prompt: What does a hardware wallet protect against?
options: Market volatility
Malware on your computer reading your private keys
Sending funds to a wrong address you approved

questions.prompt: Where should you confirm a transaction's details when using a hardware wallet?
options: On the hardware wallet's own screen
On the computer screen only
In the confirmation email

questions.prompt: A hardware wallet arrives with a seed phrase already printed in the box. You should:
options: Use it; it saves a step
Use it for small amounts only
Not use it; the device must generate a new phrase that only you have seen

questions.prompt: How do you know your backup actually works?
options: You test restoring the wallet from it before you rely on it
You assume it does; backups do not fail
You ask the wallet vendor to confirm

questions.prompt: You suspect your wallet's keys are compromised but funds are still there. First step?
options: Wait to see whether anything moves
Move the funds to a new wallet with freshly generated keys
Post the address publicly to warn others
Emailing your seed phrase to a relative
Keeping no records so nothing can be found
Written instructions a trusted person can follow, without exposing the seed phrase in advance
